text_blocks.text: Logo family
The Augur mark exists in three compositions. The horizontal lockup is
preferred for most use cases. The vertical composition is for situations where the horizontal one does not fit. The glyph stands alone as the compact expression of the identity.
All three are available in full color, single-tint dark, white, and reversed, in
PNG and SVG.
H O R I Z O N T A L · P R I M A R Y
V E R T I C A L G LY P H
W H I C H O N E
Horizontal unless the width is genuinely constrained. Vertical when it is. Glyph only where the name Augur is
already on the surface. Reaching for the vertical lockup because it looks better in the space is the common error.
O N E C H O I C E P E R S U R F A C E
Pick a composition per surface and keep it. A header, a favicon, and a slide master can each use a different
composition; the same header should not alternate between two.
N A M I N G
Files are named by variant, not by composition: Color, Black, White, Reversed sit inside a Horizontal, Vertical,
or Glyph folder. Black means Augur Navy #0E0E21, not #000000.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 7
Horizontal lockup
The primary composition. Use it wherever horizontal space allows: website headers,
documents, presentations, press material, and exchange listings.
Choose the variant by background rather than by preference. Full color on light or dark surfaces where the green holds contrast, reversed on dark surfaces, single tint where the logo is a supporting
element.
C O L O R · T W O T I N T · L I G H T S U R F A C E
A U G U R N A V Y · S I N G L E T I N T W H I T E · S I N G L E T I N T R E V E R S E D · T W O T I N T
B A C K G R O U N D F I R S T, P R E F E R E N C E S E C O N D

Read the surface, then pick the variant. Color on Paper and White. Reversed on Augur Navy. The green is the thing being protected: it carries 11.87:1 on Navy and 1.47:1 on Paper, so it can hold a mark on dark and
cannot hold one on light.
W H I T E A N D R E V E R S E D A R E N O T T H E S A M E

White is one tint, the whole mark in white. Reversed is two tints, green arrow over white wordmark. Use Reversed on Navy by default; use White where the mark is supporting and should not pull attention.
M I N I M U M W I D T H
Below 150 px wide the glyph inside this lockup falls under its own minimum. See 02.6.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 8
Vertical lockup
Use the vertical composition when the primary composition is not a good fit. It is
a fallback for constrained widths, not an alternative primary.
Typical cases are narrow columns, square placements, badge formats, and centered layouts such as event backdrops or slide covers.
The same tint rules apply as for the horizontal composition.
C O L O R A U G U R N A V Y W H I T E R E V E R S E D
I T I S A F A L L B A C K
If the horizontal lockup fits, use it. The test is whether
the horizontal mark would have to drop below its minimum to fit the space – not whether the vertical one looks better centered in it.
W H E R E I T E A R N S I T S P L A C E
Narrow columns, square and circular placements,
badge and avatar formats, event backdrops, slide covers, and any layout whose axis is already vertical.
M I N I M U M H E I G H T
The glyph sits above the wordmark at roughly half the
lockup height, so this composition needs 93 px of height to keep the glyph above its own minimum. See 02.6.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 9
Glyph
The glyph is the compact expression of the Augur identity: the arrow and pyramid
silhouette without the wordmark. Use it where the full lockup would be illegible or where the Augur name is already established by context.
When the glyph is used alone, the proportion between the glyph and adjacent elements must match the
clearspace proportion defined for the full lockup.
C O L O R A U G U R N A V Y W H I T E R E V E R S E D
V A R I A N T M A P P I N G
Color is green with navy. Reversed is green with white. White is a single white tint. The files named Black use Augur Navy #0E0E21 – there is no true black anywhere
in this system.
T W O F O R M S , O N E G A P
The glyph is an arrow above a pyramid, separated by a gap of about four percent of its height. That gap is the feature most likely to close at small sizes, which is why
the minimum in 02.6 is set where it is.
W H E N T H E G LY P H M A Y S T A N D A L O N E
Only where the name Augur is already established by the surrounding context: an app icon, a favicon, an avatar, a repeated element inside a product someone
is already using. Never as a first introduction.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 10
Clearspace
Use the lowercase a in the wordmark as the clearspace unit, written as 1a. Leave
at least one a-width on the left and right, and one a-height above and below. No element, edge, or fold may enter that zone.
When the glyph is used alone, maintain the same proportion between the glyph and any adjacent element.
The unit scales with the artwork, so there
is no separate fixed pixel or millimeter value. More clearspace is always allowed.
C L E A R S P A C E C O N S T R U C T I O N
1a
1a
Shaded band: minimum clear space. Dashed boundary: logo bounding box. The 1a labels show the horizontal and vertical clearspace units.
W H A T T H E U N I T I S
The lowercase a from the supplied wordmark. Left and right use its width; top and bottom use its height. Because the unit is drawn from the artwork it scales
with it, so one rule covers a favicon and a trade-show wall.
W H A T C O U N T S A S A N I N T R U S I O N
Any ink, any edge, and any fold. Page trim, a card boundary, a column rule, a photograph, and a neighboring logo are all intrusions. Nothing enters the
zone, including elements that are themselves quiet.
T H E G LY P H A L O N E
Keep the same proportion between the glyph and whatever sits next to it. Clearspace is defined as a ratio, not a measurement, so it does not need restating per
composition.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 11
Minimum size
The glyph may be reduced to a height of 50 px on screen, measured from the tip of
the arrow to the base of the pyramid. Use a larger size whenever the layout allows.
The controlling dimension is the pyramid, which must not fall below 24 px. Everything else on this page derives from that.
If the wordmark becomes difficult to read at a small size, use the glyph only where
the surrounding context already identifies Augur.
H O W T H E M I N I M U M I S D E R I V E D
24 px
pyramid, the controlling dimension
50 px
full glyph height, measure this

The pyramid is 48.3% of the glyph, so a pyramid of 24 px puts the whole glyph at 50 px. The shaded band is the gap between the two forms: below this size it drops under two pixels and they begin to merge.
A T T H E M I N I M U M Actual size
Glyph 50 × 45 px
Horizontal lockup 150 × 50 px
Vertical lockup 94 × 93 px
H O W T O M E A S U R E

Take the glyph’s full bounding box, arrow tip to pyramid base. Do not measure the pyramid alone unless you are checking the derivation. The same floor applies to the glyph inside a lockup, which is where the
lockup minimums above come from.
W H Y T H E L O C K U P S D I F F E R

The glyph is the same height as the horizontal lockup and a little over half the height of the vertical one, so the vertical composition needs roughly twice the height to keep its glyph legal. Composition changes
the number; the rule does not change.
B E L O W T H E M I N I M U M

There is no approved treatment. Use the glyph where context already names Augur, or give the mark more room. Do not simplify, sharpen, thicken, or redraw it to survive a smaller size – a mark redrawn to fit stops
matching the one in production.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 12
Logo color variants
The color rule has a default and two named exceptions.
The full logo may be used in one or two

tints. Two tints is the default. Use a single-tint variant only where the green has no contrast against the background or there are production limitations, or where the logo is a supporting element that does not need to draw attention,
such as in documentation or repeated on each page of a slide deck.
In those cases use the supplied single-tint Augur Navy or white variant.
T W O T I N T · D E F A U L T O N E T I N T · D A R K O N E T I N T · W H I T E
T W O T I N T · R E V E R S E D
Augur Navy is #0E0E21. It is the primary brand color and the default dark surface
throughout the system. The files named Black use this Augur Navy value – there is no true black in the palette, and substituting one will not match anything else on the surface.
T W O T I N T S I S T H E D E F A U L T
One tint is an exception with two named causes: the green has no contrast on the background, or production cannot carry two colors. Preferring the quieter look is not one of them.
T H E T H I R D C A S E
A supporting role. A mark repeated on every slide of a deck, or sitting in the corner of a documentation page, is not asking for attention and should not take it. Single tint is correct there.
D O N O T B U I L D Y O U R O W N

Every variant on this page is a supplied file. Recoloring the two-tint artwork to make a one-tint version produces a mark that is close but not identical, and the difference shows the moment the two appear
together.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 13
Approved backgrounds
This section defines which logo variant is used against each approved brand
surface while maintaining legibility and adequate contrast.
Use Color on the near-white light surface and Reversed on Augur Navy. Keep the logo on a controlled solid surface whenever imagery or a pattern would reduce its clarity.
S A F E S U R F A C E S
L I G H T S U R F A C E #F5F5F8 · U S E C O L O R N A V Y S U R F A C E #0E0E21 · U S E R E V E R S E D
W H I T E #FFFFFF · U S E C O L O R R A I S E D #242438 · U S E R E V E R S E D
F O U R S U R F A C E S , T W O V A R I A N T S
Color on the two light surfaces, Reversed on the two dark ones. Every other brand surface in section 03 is a lifted step of one of these four and takes the same
variant as its parent.
W H Y S O L I D
These pairings hold the relationship between Augur Green, Augur Navy, and white. A photograph or pattern breaks it in a way no variant choice can repair, because
the background is not one color to choose against.
W H E N T H E S U R F A C E I S N O T Y O U R S
Partner sites, listings, and press templates are uncontrolled. Place the mark on a solid brand field of your own and put that field on their surface, rather than
putting the mark straight onto whatever is there.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 14
0 2 . 9 Incorrect usage
Preserve the supplied geometry, color, clearspace, and composition. These
examples cover the most common production failures; when in doubt, return
to the approved asset rather than correcting it by eye.
D O N O T E N C L O S E O R K E Y L I N E
No border, badge, or containing shape.
D O N O T R O T A T E
Keep the wordmark on its supplied baseline.
D O N O T D I S T O R T
Scale uniformly; never stretch or compress.
D O N O T U S E A B U S Y F I E L D
Move the mark to a controlled solid field.
D O N O T U S E L O W C O N T R A S T
Choose the variant for the background.
D O N O T C R O W D C L E A R S P A C E
TEXT
Keep type, edges, and rules outside 1a.
D O N O T A D D E F F E C T S
No shadow, glow, bevel, texture, or gradient.
D O N O T A D D T A G L I N E S
P R E D I C T E V E R Y T H I N G
Keep campaigns and partner marks separate.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 15
Token icon
The REP token icon shown here is the canonical token asset.
Use the supplied PNG or SVG directly.
Keep its geometry, colors, proportions, and circular navy field unchanged. Do not redraw, recolor, crop, or add effects to the icon.
C A N O N I C A L R E P T O K E N I C O N
A complete composition
The navy circle belongs to the icon. Preserve the centered glyph, field, geometry, and color relationship exactly as supplied.
Production use
Use SVG for scalable artwork and PNG for raster environments. Keep the icon circular and allow clearspace around its outer edge.
Do not recolor
The green, white, and navy relationship is fixed. The icon is a token identity, and a recolored token reads as a different token.
Do not alter geometry
Do not redraw or change the relationship between the upper and lower forms, and do not substitute the section 02.4 glyph for the one inside the icon.
Do not remove the field
The navy circle is part of the token icon, not a presentation background. Cropping to a square, or dropping the circle to sit the glyph on your own surface, both produce a mark that is not this one.
A U G U R B R A N D F O U N D A T I O N 0 2 L O G O S Y S T E M 16
